Chapter 01

Getting Oriented

MOED keeps event planning, people, communication history, and next actions connected instead of scattering them across separate systems.

◇

The Record Model at a Glance

An Inquiry holds a possible booking while it is being qualified. Once booked, it creates an Engagement linked to an Organization and its Contacts. These records can carry Chron Log history and Follow-Up Work.

1

Use the Sidebar

The main areas are always in the left sidebar. Under Work, open Email Templates to maintain reusable engagement messages. On a narrow screen, use the menu button in the top bar and tap outside the panel or press Esc to close it.

2

Switch the Theme

Select Dark Theme or Light Theme near the bottom of the sidebar. MOED remembers the choice in this browser.

3

Open Your Account

Select your name and picture to edit your profile. Calendar, account security, this manual, and sign-out controls are grouped in the lower sidebar.

A Practical First Session

  1. 01
    Complete your profile.

    Add your name, verified email, phone, and picture in My Profile.

  2. 02
    Protect the account.

    Enroll an authenticator and store the one-time recovery codes from Account Security.

  3. 03
    Check the daily view.

    Use the Dashboard to scan upcoming engagements, assigned work, and missing details.

  4. 04
    Find the relationship.

    Open the organization and relevant contacts before an event to review relationship details, financial history, Chron, and open work.

  5. 05
    Leave a clear next action.

    When a conversation creates a commitment, record the communication in Chron and create an owned, dated task.

Browse Longer Lists

Use Records per page, where available, to choose 20, 50, or 100 records. Each list remembers your preferred size in this browser. Use the page numbers, Previous, or Next to move through results. Search and sorting apply to the full result list, so you do not need to search each page separately.

Common Action Icons

◉ViewOpen details ✎EditChange a record ▶StartBegin a task ✓CompleteFinish a task □ArchiveHide reversibly ↺RestoreReturn to active ×DeleteRemove permanently

Archive first. Archiving is reversible and keeps history. Permanent deletion is limited to administrators, requires freshly confirmed administrator access, and cannot be undone.

Chapter 02

Roles and Access

Everyone can read the shared operational picture. Editing and destructive actions are deliberately narrower.

Signed In As Editor

You can create and maintain records, tasks, financial closeouts, and engagement correspondence.

CapabilityReviewerEditorAdministrator
View records, Chron, work, map, and exportsYesYesYes
Manage own profile, calendar links, and securityYesYesYes
Create and edit inquiries, engagements, organizations, contacts, and speakersNoYesYes
Manage tasks, Chron entries, closeouts, and engagement emailNoYesYes
Add, edit, archive, and restore email templatesNoYesYes
Archive and restore shared recordsNoYesYes
Manage users, audit history, backups, and permanent deletionNoNoYes
Reviewer

Read and Export

Reviewers can inspect shared records, follow links between them, use search and filters, copy presentation briefs, view presentation and QR-code PDFs, review link statistics, and subscribe to the calendar.

Editor

Coordinate and Maintain

Editors add reviewer capabilities plus record creation, editing, archive/restore, task management, Chron maintenance, financial closeout, engagement email, and inbound email review.

Administrator

Govern and Recover

Administrators add user lifecycle controls, audit inspection, encrypted backups, permanent deletion, and access to deployment signals. Sensitive actions require fresh password and 2FA confirmation.

Daily Dashboard
html:
Chapter 03

Daily Dashboard

The Dashboard answers three questions: what is coming, what is yours, and what is incomplete.

Scan

Daily Summary

The compact top cards distinguish all active work from your own active and overdue work. Shared counts link to the booking pipeline, financial closeouts, and—when available to your role—inbound mail awaiting review.

Act

Primary Panels

My Work leads with assigned tasks by urgency and due date, alongside Upcoming Engagements. Open the Booking pipeline disclosure below Needs Attention for inquiry next actions and pipeline health.

My Work and Inquiry Next Actions show a short due date with a second line such as 1 day overdue, Due today, or Upcoming. Items more than 3 days overdue pulse red in a repeating cascade to draw your attention. For inquiries, this is based on the next-action due date.

Prepare

Event Readiness

Readiness flags an unconfirmed event, missing venue address, missing presentation, or missing event contact assignment. Open the event to complete the missing details.

Close

Financial Closeouts

Ended events remain here until actual giving/income, lodging, and travel receipts are finalized. The age indicator shows how many days the report has been waiting.

Open the Dashboard →

title: Inquiry and Booking Pipeline
html:
Chapter 04

Inquiry and Booking Pipeline

Use an Inquiry for a possible event that is not booked yet. It keeps early communication and follow-up visible without creating a partly known Engagement.

↗

Inquiry First, Engagement After Booking

The Inquiry is the source record for qualification. Converting it creates the Engagement once an organization, title, and preferred date range are known. The original Inquiry then becomes read-only and remains linked for reference.

Work the Pipeline

  1. 01
    Capture the request.

    Select New Inquiry in the Booking Pipeline. Add the organization and contact when known; they can remain blank during early triage.

  2. 02
    Assign the next action.

    Choose an owner and priority, then state the concrete next step and its due date. The pipeline cards and Dashboard emphasize this action.

  3. 03
    Move the stage.

    Use New → Contacted → Qualified → Awaiting Details → Proposal Sent as the normal path. Move backward when the facts warrant it. Declining requires a reason and can be reopened later.

  4. 04
    Keep the history together.

    Open the Inquiry and use the Activity, Correspondence, and Tasks tabs to keep decisions, email, and follow-up work together. Open a message from Correspondence to review delivery or retry a failed delivery while the Inquiry is active.

  5. 05
    Review the booking.

    Select Convert to Engagement when the request is ready. Check the imported engagement details, availability warnings, and which open tasks should move. Clearing every task checkbox moves none. If a next action remains, explicitly carry it forward as a task or resolve it with a reason; the original action and your decision remain in history. Warnings require acknowledgement but remain a deliberate, auditable decision.

  6. 06
    Continue in the Engagement.

    Conversion creates the Engagement, assigns the Inquiry’s primary contact as Primary Host when available, moves selected work, and adds the standard event checklist. Replies to earlier Inquiry correspondence continue into the converted Engagement.

Triage

Filter the Board

Search request text, organizations, contacts, and locations. Use the owner and next-action filters to find your inquiries, unassigned work, overdue actions, or requests that still need a next step.

Communicate

Use the Starting Templates

Initial response, request details, date options, and proposal follow-up templates are editable before sending. Sent messages appear in Correspondence and Chron with delivery status.

Protect History

Keep the Source Record

Do not copy pre-booking Chron Log Entries by hand. The booked Inquiry retains its source email, stage history, Chron, correspondence, and any work not moved to the Engagement. Resolve or reassign active Inquiries before archiving their Contact or Organization.

The default board shows active inquiries and those booked this month. Use the Stage filter for Booked, Declined, or All Stages. In All Stages, Declined starts on a separate row. The stages wrap to fit your screen; scroll down to see the remaining rows.

Open the Booking Pipeline →

html:
Chapter 05

Engagements

An engagement is the operational record for one event: the schedule, assigned people, presentations, logistics, planning state, communication history, work, and final receipts.

Find and Read an Engagement

Search Broadly

The Engagements search checks event titles and descriptions, organizations, contacts, caller names, active Chron text, and Chron authors. Unquoted words are alternatives; words inside one quoted group must all match. Terms shorter than three characters are ignored.

Exampleconference "travel confirmed"

Filter Precisely

Switch between current and archived records, filter by lifecycle, then sort by organization, date, confirmation, or lifecycle. The summary cards show current lifecycle totals.

The table shows event dates, lifecycle, confirmation, and whether financial closeout is open, closed, or not applicable. Select the title or View icon for the full record.

Create or Edit an Engagement

  1. 01
    Choose the organization.

    The event must belong to one active organization. If it is new, create the organization first.

  2. 02
    Name and schedule the event.

    Enter a required event title, an optional description, a valid start and end date, and an event type. Use Other when the preset types do not fit.

  3. 03
    Assign event contacts.

    Select multiple existing contacts and give each any applicable event roles: Primary host, On-site contact, Billing, Travel, or Materials. Search the directory to add another person, or use Add new contact repeatedly. New contacts and organization affiliations are saved with the event.

  4. 04
    Add presentations.

    Choose a saved speaker from the dropdown; add missing speakers in Relationships → Speakers. Presentation details can be filled in later. Dates must fall within the event range, and duration is entered in minutes. Record actual attendance afterward, including zero when applicable. At least one complete presentation is required before the engagement can be Confirmed.

  5. 05
    Capture logistics.

    Record book-table and brochure permissions, travel coverage, planned compensation, travel/lodging estimates, lodging type, and the physical event location.

  6. 06
    Set planning states and ownership.

    Choose lifecycle and confirmation, then select the Caller when that person should own the initial standard checklist. If no Caller is selected, the checklist belongs to the user creating the engagement. Add an initial Chron entry when there is context worth preserving.

Create a New Engagement →

Operational State

Lifecycle

Active
The event is moving forward.
Postponed
The original is paused and may link to its replacement.
Canceled
A reason is required; open event tasks are canceled automatically.
Completed
The event has finished. Finalizing its financial report also sets this state.
Planning Confidence

Confirmation

Work in Progress
Details are still being assembled.
Under Review
The plan is ready for checking or decision.
Confirmed
The commitment is agreed and at least one complete presentation exists.

Lifecycle and confirmation are independent. A postponed event can retain its former confirmation state, while a completed event may reflect the confirmation state it reached during planning.

Presentation Files, QR Codes, and History

PDF Speaker Notes

Attach one PDF up to 100 MB to each presentation with Choose PDF, then save. Select View PDF Speaker Notes on the event detail page to open it in a new tab. Use Replace PDF or Remove current PDF on the edit page and save to update it.

Use this file for notes you intend to share: anyone with its QR code can open the PDF without signing in.

Speaker QR Codes

Saving creates separate codes for each presentation’s available speaker resources: website, bio, donations, connection, blog, books, custom links, and notes. Select a displayed code to copy it. Download PNG or SVG images when you prefer to save a file for your slides or handouts.

The Speaker Notes code appears after its PDF is saved. Replacing the PDF keeps the same code. Removing the file hides the code; adding notes again reuses the code and its statistics.

Select View QR Codes PDF to view, save, or print a single landscape sheet of that presentation’s labeled codes, schedule, and venue. Missing schedule details show To be confirmed. Disabled codes are labeled; notes without a PDF and previous speakers’ codes are left out. Viewing the sheet does not add visits.

Each saved presentation has a nearby Save Changes button. It saves the engagement form, including other changes on the page. Presentations can be archived and restored separately from the event. When restoring, update any date that falls outside the event’s current date range. Administrators can permanently delete presentations after confirming their access.

When postponing or canceling an event, link it to a replacement from the same organization. MOED displays both “rescheduled as” and “rescheduled from” references and prevents circular links.

Manage Email Templates

Open Email Templates under Work in the sidebar, or select Manage Email Templates in the engagement email composer. This library supplies engagement email in the browser and Mattermost. Inquiry emails use their own starting templates.

  1. 01
    Add or edit a template.

    Select + New Email Template, or open an active template by its name or Edit action. Enter the template name, subject, and plain-text message. The original Booking confirmation, Travel and lodging request, Final-detail reconfirmation, Presentation schedule, and Post-event thank-you templates can all be edited.

  2. 02
    Personalize the starting text.

    Expand Personalize with event fields. Click where the field belongs in the subject or message, then choose a field button. Event name, organization, dates, location, and speaker names are available; Presentation schedule belongs in the message only. For example, Welcome to {{event_name}} uses that engagement's event name when composing. The routing marker is added automatically.

  3. 03
    Choose suggestions and order.

    Select the event contact roles to suggest when this template is chosen. Leave them clear to choose contacts when composing. Lower Display order numbers appear first. Speakers are always a separate sender choice; inserting Speaker names into the message does not add recipients.

  4. 04
    Save and review.

    Select Create Template or Save Changes. Choose the saved template in an engagement email to review the filled subject, message, and recipients before queuing. When you entered the library from an engagement, Return to Email takes you back to its composer.

Archive and Restore

Search the library by name or subject. Archive removes a template from new emails in both composers. Open Archived to view it or select Restore to make it available again. Restore an archived template before editing it.

Delete and Access

Editors and administrators can add, edit, archive, and restore templates. Reviewers can view them. Only administrators can permanently Delete an archived template, after confirming their access. Deletion cannot be undone; sent messages, their template names, and Chron history remain available.

Changes apply to future messages. A draft already open in a composer keeps its reviewed text. If its template is archived or deleted before sending, review the preserved draft as Custom message or choose another template. If another session changed a template while you were editing, keep a copy of your draft, reload, and review the latest version before saving. Custom message is always available, even when every saved template is archived.

Review QR Code Activity

  • In the Presentations tab, select Statistics beneath a code to see its visits. Open a speaker’s record and choose Statistics for activity across that speaker’s presentations.
  • Choose a date range to focus on a recent event or a longer period. In the speaker view, use Link Type to focus on notes, donations, or Custom Links, then select Apply Filters.
  • Use the charts to see when and where links were opened. Hover or tap for details, or expand the data tables for exact counts. These are visits to links, not an attendance count. Speaker Notes records the link visit before opening the PDF, including cached delivery; opening a copied direct PDF address does not add a visit.

To change where an existing code leads, editors and administrators can open that code’s Statistics, edit Destination, and select Save Link. The printed code continues to work. Clear Link enabled and save to stop access through that code. For Speaker Notes, replace the PDF on the presentation instead of editing a destination.

Editing a speaker’s profile does not change destinations already shared with audiences. Previous speakers’ links and notes remain separate when you change a presentation’s speaker.

Send and Track Event Email

Editors and administrators can send email from an active engagement. Use Send Email near the page heading or Send Message in the Correspondence section. Every message remains easy to find there afterward.

  1. 01
    Choose a starting template.

    Choose an active template from the shared library, or Custom message to write from scratch. Event fields are filled from this engagement. Template text is only a starting point; edit the subject and body before sending. Use Manage Email Templates to learn how to maintain the library.

  2. 02
    Select recipients.

    Use the Primary host, On-site contact, Billing, Travel, Materials, or Speaker shortcuts, or select individual recipient cards. Speakers assigned to active presentations are optional and unchecked by default. Choose the Speaker shortcut or check a speaker card to include them. You may send to speakers alone. Changing templates keeps your speaker selection. Only assigned contacts and speakers with a valid email address can receive the message. Every unique address receives a separate email, so recipients never see one another. A speaker and contact sharing one address receive only one copy.

  3. 03
    Review the routing marker.

    The exact engagement marker is included in every template subject and is added automatically if removed. When inbound mail is enabled, replies return through the shared mailbox and the marker helps place them in the right engagement Chron.

  4. 04
    Optionally append the event brief.

    The share-safe brief includes the public event schedule, venue, description, and presentations. It deliberately excludes Chron, internal notes, compensation, giving, and financial-closeout information. Preview it before queuing.

  5. 05
    Send and check the result.

    Select Queue Email, then use the Correspondence list to see whether each recipient is waiting, sent, or failed. If a recipient remains failed, open the message and select Retry Failed Deliveries.

One Place to Check

Open the outbound message to review what was sent, who it was sent to, and the result for each address.

Automatic Chron History

The message is added to the Engagement, Organization, and selected Contact Chron logs. Select View Outbound Message from a Chron entry to return to its delivery record.

View, Share, and Close the Event

The event detail page shows its unique email routing marker. The built-in outbound composer inserts it automatically. When using another mail application, select the copy icon immediately beside the marker and keep it in the email subject or plain-text body when that message should route to the engagement’s Chron log.

In the Presentations tab, open Export Presentation at the bottom of a presentation card. Briefs include that presentation’s speaker, schedule, duration, and attendance, with its event and venue context.

Copy Text

Copies a plain-text presentation brief for messages or notes.

Copy MD

Copies a Markdown-formatted presentation brief for systems that support structured text.

View PDF

Opens a branded brief for the selected presentation in your browser for viewing, saving, or printing.

View QR Codes PDF

Opens a themed landscape sheet containing only that presentation’s labeled QR codes.

Editors and administrators can use Financial Closeout to save a receipt draft while work is still pending. Leave unknown amounts blank; enter zero only when nothing was received. Drafts are excluded from finalized financial history. The original planning estimates remain unchanged. Every event task due on or before the last active presentation must first be marked Completed; canceled tasks still block until truthfully resolved, while later and undated tasks do not hold closeout. Confirm that the amounts are final to complete the engagement; later corrections retain the original close date and record the update.

!

Archive and Delete Carefully

Archive removes the engagement from current views but keeps its history available for restoration. Permanent deletion removes the event and all event-specific information, including presentations, Chron, tasks, contact role assignments, and its financial report. Prefer archive unless removal is explicitly required.

Open Engagements →

Organizations, Contacts, and Speakers
html:
Chapter 06

Organizations, Contacts, and Speakers

Organizations hold relationship history, contacts identify the people involved, and speaker profiles keep presentation details and audience resources ready to reuse.

Organization

Relationship Record

Store the organization name, notes, affiliation, distinctives, website, phone, fax, and physical and mailing addresses. You can use one address for both or maintain them separately.

Only the organization name is required; add address and relationship details when known. A new organization can create its first contact at the same time, and can add more contacts before saving.

Add an organization
Contact

Person Record

Store first and last name, optional primary organization, additional organization affiliations with their own roles or titles, email, phone, incidental notes, and an optional JPEG, PNG, or WebP photo up to 5 MB. A contact can be saved without an organization. Use Create Organization in the contact form to add a missing organization without losing the contact details or selected photo.

The organization role is Pastor, Admin, or Other. When you choose Other, enter the custom description in Describe Other Role beside the Role field. Additional organizations each have their own role or title, such as Pastor at a church and Chairman at a research center. Event-specific roles are assigned separately on each engagement.

Add a contact

Enter Organization Addresses

  • Choose the country before the region. The Country picker includes countries worldwide and defaults to United States of America for a new address.
  • For a United States address, the region field is labeled State and provides a dropdown of state names.
  • For a Canadian address, the region field is labeled Province and provides a dropdown of province and territory names.
  • For every other country, the field is labeled State/Province and accepts typed regional information.
  • The same behavior applies to both physical and mailing addresses. Select Same as Physical Address when the mailing address does not differ.

Lists, Details, and Financial History

  • Search organizations by their details or active contacts; sort by name and switch between Active and Archived.
  • The organization list shows location, active contacts, last giving, and lifetime giving from finalized reports.
  • An organization detail page summarizes lifetime giving, last and average event giving, lodging, travel, and recent finalized reports.
  • Search contacts by person or organization, sort by last name or organization, and choose 20, 50, or 100 records per page.
  • A contact detail page links to all its organizations and shows that person’s Chron and open follow-up work.

Keep Speaker Profiles Ready to Use

Open Relationships → Speakers to find a speaker by name, email, or phone. Select Name to switch alphabetical order, then open the speaker’s name or View icon for their details. Administrators and editors can use New Speaker or Edit Speaker; reviewers can view profiles and statistics.

  • Save the speaker’s name, email address, and phone number once, then choose that speaker when adding presentations.
  • Add a biography and an optional photo to make the profile useful and recognizable. Photos can be JPEG, PNG, or WebP, up to 5 MB.
  • Add the speaker’s website and other audience links. The written Bio is for the profile; Bio URL is the web page opened by the biography QR code.
  • For videos, social pages, or other resources, use Speakers → Edit Speaker → Custom Links. Give each link a clear name and full web address; select Add Custom Link for more, then Save speaker.

Saving a new custom link adds a separate QR code to that speaker’s existing presentations, and future presentations receive their own codes. Renaming or removing a profile link keeps already-published links and their statistics intact. To change or disable a shared code, select Statistics beneath that code on its presentation.

Speakers remain available permanently and cannot be archived or deleted. Keep their existing profiles current instead of creating duplicates.

i

Organization Archive Rule

An organization cannot be archived while it still has active contacts or engagements. Archive those child records first, or move them to another active organization. Restoring a contact or engagement also requires its organization to be active.

OrganizationsSearch and review relationship records → ContactsFind people and communication history → SpeakersMaintain profiles and audience resources →

title: Work Queue
html:
Chapter 07

Work Queue

Tasks turn relationship context into an explicit next action with an owner, timing, priority, and state. They may stay attached to an Inquiry until selected work moves during booking.

My Reminders

The sidebar badge and Dashboard personal cards always count your own reminders. In the queue, choose Mine, Everyone, or Unassigned; every queue summary count uses that same ownership scope, search, and related-record filter.

Queue Views

Choose an ownership scope, then filter Active, Overdue, Due Today, Next 7 Days, Waiting, or Completed. The Dashboard’s My Overdue Work card opens Overdue limited to your assignments. Search matches task content, related records, and assignees.

Due Dates and Overdue Pulses

The due date appears as a short date, such as Sep 4, with a second line showing the number of days overdue, Due today, or Upcoming. Days are counted by calendar date in the application’s time zone. Priority and workflow status appear separately.

Active tasks more than 3 days overdue—starting at 4 days overdue—have a pulsing red row background. When several items qualify, the pulse moves down the list in a repeating cascade, with each pulse overlapping the next. Tasks 1–3 days overdue keep a steady red highlight; tasks due today have a blue highlight. Completed and canceled tasks do not pulse.

The same attention cues appear in the Dashboard’s My Work and Inquiry Next Actions lists. An active inquiry qualifies when its next-action due date is more than 3 days overdue.

Hovering over a row, or moving keyboard focus to a control within it, shows an orange highlight over the pulse so you can clearly follow the item you are using. The pulse becomes visible again when the pointer and focus leave the row. If your device or browser prefers reduced motion, overdue items use a steady stronger red highlight instead of blinking.

Create a Useful Task

  1. 01
    Write a concrete title.

    Use notes for supporting detail, not as a substitute for the next action.

  2. 02
    Link the right record.

    Search for an engagement, organization, or contact; choose General MOED work when no record applies.

  3. 03
    Name an owner and due date.

    Tasks may be unassigned or have no date, but explicit ownership keeps them out of limbo.

  4. 04
    Set priority and status.

    Choose Low, Normal, High, or Urgent and one of the workflow states below.

StatusUse It WhenWhat Happens Next
OpenThe task is known but not started.Start it, complete it, or edit the owner/timing.
In ProgressSomeone is actively working it.Complete it or move it to Waiting if blocked.
WaitingProgress depends on a person, organization, or decision.The “Waiting on” description becomes required.
CompletedThe action is finished.It moves to Completed and can be reopened.
CanceledThe action is no longer needed.It leaves active views and can be reopened.

Duplicate a Task to Another Event

  1. 01
    Open the task for editing.

    Select Duplicate to Another Event at the bottom of the Edit Task page.

  2. 02
    Choose the destination event.

    Enter at least three characters in Search events, then select a different event from the results. The source event cannot be selected as its own destination.

  3. 03
    Review the copied work.

    The title, notes, assignee, due date, and priority are copied so you can adjust them before saving. The duplicate starts Open, and any “Waiting on” text is cleared.

  4. 04
    Create the duplicate.

    Select Duplicate task to add a new task to the destination event. The original task remains unchanged.

Fast Actions and Record-Level Work

From the queue, editors and administrators can assign an unowned task to themselves, start, complete, reopen, edit, or—administrators only—delete it. Engagement, organization, and contact detail pages show their open tasks in Follow-Up Work, where you can add a task or open a filtered queue.

Standard Event Tasks

Standard tasks are reusable definitions copied when a new active engagement is first saved. Each has content, priority, display order, and a due date offset from event start or end.

If the new engagement has a selected Caller, every initial standard task is assigned to that Caller. If no Caller is selected, the tasks are assigned to the user creating the engagement. This ownership decision happens only once: changing the engagement’s Caller later does not reassign its initial tasks, which remain independently editable.

Changing an engagement’s dates reschedules its active generated tasks from the standard schedule. A task whose due date was manually overridden keeps that date. Editing a standard definition does not rewrite an existing task’s title, notes, priority, or current due date.

Editors and administrators manage reusable definitions from Standard Event Tasks. Use Add Missing Checklist Tasks on an active engagement to generate any standard items that are absent; tasks added this way are assigned to the user performing the action. The built-in financial closeout reminder is fixed at one week after event end and cannot be edited, archived, or deleted.

Sending a booking, reconfirmation, or thank-you message from an engagement does not complete its related checklist task automatically. Check the Correspondence result, then complete the task when the follow-up itself is finished.

Manage Standard Event Tasks

Open the Work Queue →

html:
Chapter 08

Chron and Email

Chron is the durable communication history. Add concise Chron Log Entries directly, send tracked engagement correspondence, or route copied inbound email into the relevant records.

Use the Chron Log

  • Use Add Chron Log Entry on an inquiry, engagement, organization, or contact to save activity without editing the full record. Contact Chron records communication with that person only; Organization Chron records organization-level history; Engagement Chron records event-specific planning.
  • Entries show created time and author, newest first. Edited entries also show the last update time and editor.
  • Editors and administrators add, edit, and archive entries from the record’s edit page. Administrators can permanently delete them.
  • Restore archived entries in batches from the Restore page. An archived parent record must be active before its Chron can be restored.
  • Email-generated entries link to their retained inbound or outbound source message while it exists.
Send

Start from an Engagement

Open an active engagement and select Send Message. Choose assigned contacts, review the message, and send. The engagement marker and related Chron history are handled for you. Check the Correspondence section for the result.

Receive

Route Outside Email

When using another mail application, copy the inbound address and keep the exact engagement marker in the subject or plain-text body: [MOED#123.<signed-token>]. Use the copy icon beside the marker on the engagement page.

How Inbound Email Finds Its Records

One unique, valid signed engagement marker routes directly to that active engagement only when the sender also uniquely matches an active record. Unknown senders and unsigned legacy markers require review. When participant matching is uncertain, only the signed engagement receives the Chron entry.

Address Matching

MOED matches exact email addresses for active verified users, contacts, and organizations. A unique contact participant routes to the Contact and its Organization. A direct organization address routes there. Cc and Bcc delivery both work.

What Inbound Mail Retains

The Chron entry includes normalized headers, subject, timestamps, inert plain-text body, attachment names, and a source link. Attachment contents are not stored. Duplicate delivery of the same message ID is ignored.

Review the Inbound Queue

Editors and administrators see messages grouped as Needs review, Pending, Processing, Failed, Processed, or Rejected. Without a valid signed marker, every message requires review. Unknown or ambiguous senders, shared addresses, messages with no unique target, and invalid, conflicting, unknown, or archived engagement markers also require review.

  1. 01
    Inspect the source.

    Open Inbox in the sidebar. On a wide screen, the message list is on the left, the reader is in the middle, and the filing panel is on the right. Search by subject, sender, or content; use Order and the queue pages to find a message. Needs review starts oldest first. Selecting a message keeps Search messages visible at the same vertical position. Expand Message details for recipients, sent time, and attachment names, or Routing details for matching reasons. On a phone, use Back to messages to return to the list.

  2. 02
    Choose the Chron Logs.

    In the filing panel, review the reason under Review needed. Select the intended Contact, Organization, or Inquiry suggestions when available. Find an active engagement by name, ID, or email marker and choose it from the Engagement list. Check the count of selected Chron logs before saving.

  3. 03
    Choose an outcome.

    Save to Chron logs saves the conversation to the selected records. Find matches again checks routing again after record corrections. Expand Other actions to Reject message while retaining the source without writing Chron. For a processed message, review Message status and Saved to Chron to confirm where it was filed.

Open Inbound Mail →

!

Treat Address Matching as a Routing Aid

An exact visible From address is not independent proof of identity. Respect the mailbox provider’s spam and SPF/DKIM/DMARC signals. Leave suspicious messages for review. Administrators can expand Manage retained email below the reader and choose Purge Mail Entry after confirmation. Purge removes the retained MOED mail card and source links, but preserves Chron entries and never deletes the original IMAP message.

Chapter 09

Map and Calendar

Use the map for geographic planning, the graphical month calendar for events and due work, and private subscription links for an external calendar application.

Explore

Engagement Map

The initial view shows active engagements in a bounded date window. Filter by lifecycle, confirmation, and date. Pin colors show confirmation, with lifecycle shown by the outline or symbol. Select a pin for the event, organization, dates, lifecycle, and a link to details.

Use Fit visible pins after filtering. The companion list includes On map, Needs address, Awaiting lookup, and Not located views for the current page, with Edit location links. Find missing addresses searches the selected date and lifecycle scope; Previous and Next reach additional pages. A new address may take time to resolve.

Open the map
View

Monthly Calendar

The Calendar page opens to the current month. Use Previous and Next to move one month at a time, or Today to return to the current month.

The current day has its own rose-colored cell and Today badge, distinct from every event and task color.

Select an event to open its details. Tasks with due dates link to task work; editors and administrators return to the same calendar view after editing.

Open the month view
Subscribe

Private Calendar

Create a separate subscription for each device or service. The secret URL is shown only once; copy it or open it directly in a calendar app. The feed contains all-day engagement blocks plus timed presentation entries using each presentation’s recorded duration.

Revoke one link without affecting the others. Revoked token records can be purged. Never share a subscription URL: it grants access to schedule data, though not contacts, Chron, travel, lodging, or compensation.

Manage calendar links

Choose What the Month Calendar Shows

SelectorCalendar ContentColor Coding
EventsEngagements that overlap the displayed dates.Event color, with distinct border tones for tentative/postponed, canceled, and completed events.
My TasksYour active tasks that have a due date in the displayed calendar grid.Your task accent color.
All TasksEvery active due-dated task in the grid, including unassigned work.Your tasks use the accent color; other or unassigned tasks use a contrasting color.

The selected filter remains active as you move between months. The summary above the grid reports how many matching events and tasks fall in that month.

title: Profile and Security
html:
Chapter 10

Profile and Security

Your profile makes ownership recognizable; the security controls protect your identity and provide safe recovery paths.

Profile and Notifications

Add your name, phone, email, and optional profile picture. Changing email clears its verified state and pauses the daily digest until the new address is verified. Resending verification preserves the profile draft and chosen photo; disabled digest schedules do not require a delivery time or day.

A verified email enables password recovery and a Dashboard-style Daily Digest of upcoming engagements, My Work, event readiness, and financial closeouts. Overdue and due-today tasks are highlighted, and editor/admin digests also include inbound mail awaiting review. The digest defaults to enabled on weekdays at 7:00 a.m.; disable it or choose a different time and set of days at any time.

Open My Profile

Password Rules

Passwords must contain at least 12 characters and no more than 72 UTF-8 bytes. Changing your password signs out every other session. If an administrator gives you a temporary password, you must replace it before using other areas.

Open Account Security

Set Up Two-Factor Authentication

  1. 01
    Confirm your password.

    If replacing an existing authenticator, also enter a current code.

  2. 02
    Add the account.

    Scan the QR code in your authenticator app or enter the manual setup key.

  3. 03
    Verify enrollment.

    Enter the six-digit code generated by the app.

  4. 04
    Save recovery codes.

    Each code works once and the page will not show them again. Store them in an approved password manager or another secure location.

At sign-in, enter either the current six-digit authenticator code or one unused recovery code. Generating new recovery codes invalidates all old ones. Administrators must keep 2FA enabled; other roles may disable it after password and current-code confirmation.

Recover Access

  • Forgotten password: choose “Forgot your password?” on sign-in and enter the verified email on the active account. The single-use link lets you set a new password and invalidates existing sessions.
  • Lost authenticator: use one saved recovery code at the 2FA prompt, then replace the authenticator and generate a fresh set of codes.
  • No recovery factor: contact an administrator. They can issue a temporary password or reset another user’s 2FA after elevated confirmation; they cannot reveal an old password or recovery code.
  • New account: open the invitation link within seven days, create a private password, and complete required authenticator enrollment.

html:
Chapter 11

Mattermost

The MOED plugin brings daily summaries, engagement context, follow-up actions, and carefully reviewed engagement email into Mattermost while MOED remains the system of record.

◇

Link Your Account First

Open Mattermost in MOED and generate a one-time code. The code is shown once, expires after 10 minutes, and becomes invalid after use. In Mattermost, run /moed connect CODE. Command responses are private to you. Never paste the code into an ordinary channel message.

Commands

CommandWhat It DoesWho Can Use It
/moed helpShows the command reference and account-linking reminder.Everyone
/moed statusChecks the plugin connection and reports which MOED account is linked.Everyone
/moed connect CODEConsumes a one-time code from the MOED Mattermost page and links your identities.Everyone
/moed todayShows a private dashboard with Overdue, Due today, Next 7 days, and Waiting counts, active assigned tasks, and a link back to MOED.Linked users
/moed tasksShows the same task dashboard with up to 15 active tasks assigned to you. Editors and administrators also receive permitted action buttons.Linked users
/moed event search TEXTSearches active and historical non-archived engagements by event or organization name.Linked users
/moed event show IDShows a private engagement card with dates, status, location, work counts, and an email routing marker you can copy.Linked users
/moed link-event IDBinds the current channel to an engagement, adds its routing marker to the channel name, and posts its card.Editors and administrators with native channel-management and posting permission
/moed unlink-eventRemoves the channel’s engagement binding and its channel-name marker.Editors and administrators with native channel-management and posting permission
Channel Context

Engagement Cards

Run /moed event show ID for a private engagement card. Linking a channel posts the same useful engagement context for the channel. Both cards show the email routing marker with a Copy control so it can be kept in a related email subject or message. Use Open in MOED for the complete record.

Follow-Up

Task Buttons

Editors and administrators can assign an unowned task to themselves, start it, complete it, or reopen it. Each button checks the task version before changing MOED; if someone already changed the task, refresh with /moed tasks. Waiting details, reassignment to someone else, editing, cancellation, and deletion remain in MOED.

Recognize the Engagement Linked to a Channel

On desktop and mobile, a linked channel’s sidebar label begins with a compact marker such as [MOED#17], leaving more room for the channel title. The full signed routing marker remains available in engagement cards and email tools wherever it is needed for routing. The colored chain control provides the same link signal; select it, or choose MOED engagement from the channel menu, to see the engagement, open it in MOED, copy its routing marker, or begin an email. Unlinking removes the marker from the channel name.

Send Engagement Email From Mattermost

  1. 01
    Start from the right engagement.

    In a linked channel, select the MOED chain icon and choose Send MOED email. To include a particular conversation, open that post's Message actions and choose Send via MOED email.

  2. 02
    Choose a starting point.

    Select an active template from the shared Email Templates library, or Custom message, then choose from the contacts already assigned to the engagement. To include an assigned speaker, use the engagement email composer in MOED. Each unique address receives a separate message.

  3. 03
    Decide what to include.

    Edit the subject and message. You may append the share-safe event brief and, when you started from a post, the selected post or a short thread excerpt.

  4. 04
    Review before sending.

    Check the recipients, routing marker, subject, message, and any added context on the review screen. Nothing is sent until you choose Send and add to Chron.

  5. 05
    Confirm the result.

    The form shows whether each delivery is pending, sent, or failed and links to the full delivery record in MOED. The message is also recorded in the Engagement, Organization, and selected Contact Chron logs.

  6. 06
    Watch for replies.

    When a marked reply is routed back to the engagement, the MOED bot privately notifies the Mattermost user who most recently emailed that person about the engagement. Open the notification to continue in the engagement Chron.

Turn a Mattermost Post Into MOED Work

  1. 01
    Link the channel.

    An editor or administrator runs /moed link-event ID. The link establishes which engagement receives work from that channel.

  2. 02
    Open Message actions.

    Hover over a channel post and choose Message actions using the grid/apps icon—not the three-dot menu. Then choose Add MOED task, Add to MOED Chron, or Send via MOED email.

  3. 03
    Review before saving or sending.

    Confirm the task, Chron entry, or email details in the form. Nothing changes in MOED and no email is sent until you submit the final review.

  4. 04
    Continue in MOED.

    The resulting task, Chron entry, or email delivery record appears on the linked engagement, with the selected Mattermost context when you chose to include it.

Add MOED Task

Create Follow-Up Work

Add MOED task creates follow-up work on the engagement linked to the channel. MOED suggests a title and notes from the post. Review them, choose a due date and priority if needed, then save. The task appears with the engagement's other work in MOED.

Add to MOED Chron

Preserve Context as History

Add to MOED Chron adds the post to the linked engagement's history. Review or edit the suggested entry, then choose Save to Chron. Use this for decisions, outcomes, commitments, and useful conversation context that should remain with the engagement.

Send via MOED Email

Continue the Conversation

Send via MOED email creates a reviewed message to assigned engagement contacts. You can include the selected post or a short thread excerpt, and MOED keeps the routing marker, delivery result, and Chron history together.

Read the Receipt Reactions

  • 📝 Chron receipt: the MOED bot adds the :memo: reaction after Add to MOED Chron successfully writes the selected post to the linked engagement.
  • ✉️ Email receipt: the MOED bot adds the :email: reaction when a MOED email includes the selected post or thread and at least one recipient delivery succeeds.
  • Both may appear: the reactions are independent, so one post can show both. They are visual receipts rather than counters; MOED remains the authoritative record.
  • New actions only: reactions appear for Chron saves and email deliveries completed after this feature is deployed. Earlier Chron entries and emails are not marked retroactively.
✓

Before You Save

Task, Chron, and email actions all show what will be saved or sent. They are available in channels linked to a MOED engagement when your account has permission. Opening, reviewing, or canceling a form changes nothing.

Permissions, Privacy, and Unlinking

  • MOED decides access: linking does not grant a new role. Reviewers stay read only; editors and administrators receive only the task actions their MOED role permits.
  • Private by default: personal summaries, searches, email forms, delivery results, reply alerts, errors, and action confirmations are visible only to the requesting user. link-event deliberately posts a channel-visible engagement card, including its routing marker and Copy control.
  • MOED is authoritative: task, Chron, and email actions use MOED's permissions, delivery service, and records. The plugin does not connect to the MOED database or keep a second copy of engagement email.
  • Post actions are scoped: the plugin verifies that you can read the selected post and obtains the engagement from the channel's link. MOED permits task, Chron, and email actions only for linked editors and administrators.
  • Remove access: open Mattermost in MOED and choose Unlink. The Mattermost account immediately loses command access until it is linked again.
keywords: mattermost moed plugin slash command connect link account code today tasks dashboard event search show link-event unlink-event channel engagement indicator chain card routing marker copy context menu create task save chron send email template recipient post thread preview delivery reply notification reaction receipt memo button assign start complete reopen permission reviewer editor administrator open in moed privacy
title: Mattermost
Administration
html:
Chapter 12

Administration

Administrator tools control identity, accountability, continuity, and deployment health. Use them deliberately and keep a second administrator available.

Unlock Sensitive Actions

On Users—or when a destructive action redirects for confirmation—enter the administrator password plus a fresh authenticator or recovery code. Elevation lasts five minutes, and some lifecycle actions consume it immediately. Locked user controls remain hidden until confirmation succeeds.

Identity

Users

Invite a username, verified-on-acceptance email, and Reviewer, Editor, or Admin role. Review account status, profile, email verification, 2FA, password-change requirement, and activity timestamps.

Elevated actions can resend invitations, edit username, role, and daily work digest settings, set a temporary password, reset another user’s 2FA, deactivate/activate, or delete an invited or inactive account. Deactivation revokes sessions and calendar links and unassigns tasks; activation does not restore those links or assignments.

Manage users
Accountability

Audit Log

Inspect login, security, and database-change activity with actor, affected record, IP address, and local/UTC time. Filter by category, text, date range, and exact IP. Entries are newest first and append-only during normal use; individual records cannot be edited or deleted.

In the Retention panel, administrators choose how many days to keep and preview the exact UTC cutoff and affected count. Pruning requires freshly confirmed administrator access, the literal PRUNE phrase, and a final themed in-app confirmation. Deployment operators can use ./scripts/prune_audit_log.sh DAYS for the equivalent preview-first terminal workflow. Either path records the completed operation in the log.

Review the audit log
Continuity

Encrypted Backup

Confirm the administrator password and a fresh factor, then choose and confirm a unique backup password of at least 16 characters. MOED downloads the encrypted snapshot as a .dnrbackup file.

Keep the file, its password, and the separate DNR 2FA encryption key securely backed up. None can be recovered from the others. Database restore is intentionally a deployment-host procedure, not a web action.

Export a backup
Health

Operations

The internal operations view summarizes task backlog, geocoding retries, inbound mail review/failures, recent authentication failures, migration readiness, and the last encrypted backup. Use it to identify operational work that needs attention before it becomes a user-facing problem.

Open operations
!

Permanent Means Permanent

Deleting an organization preserves contacts who have another organization affiliation, and removes its remaining contacts and engagements together with their Chron, tasks, presentations, contact assignments, and financial reports. Deleting an engagement removes the same event-specific data. Deleting a contact removes that contact’s Chron, tasks, and event role assignments. Active users must be deactivated before deletion; pending invitations can be deleted directly. Use archive for ordinary record retirement.

html:
Chapter 13

Troubleshooting and Good Practice

Most surprises come from role limits, archived parent records, delayed background work, or intentionally strict safety checks.

I Cannot See an Edit or Delete Button+

Reviewers are read only. Editors can edit and archive but cannot permanently delete. Administrators must freshly unlock sensitive access before many delete and user-management controls appear. Archived records are viewed separately and generally must be restored before editing.

An Organization Will Not Archive+

Archive or move every active contact and engagement belonging to it first. MOED prevents archiving the parent while active child records would become stranded.

Search Did Not Find an Engagement+

Use terms of at least three characters. Remove quotation marks to match any word; quote a group when all its words must match. Check the Archived view and the lifecycle filter. Search indexes active Chron entries, not archived ones.

A New Address Has No Map Pin+

Confirm that the engagement contains a usable location and fits the current lifecycle/date filters. New addresses are processed asynchronously; keep the Map page open and the pin will appear automatically when the lookup finishes. If it remains pending, ask an administrator to check the geocoding queue and provider health.

An Email Still Needs Review+

Confirm the sender or participant address exactly matches one active record. Correct missing contact/organization email data, preserve a single valid [MOED#ID.<signed-token>] marker in the subject or plain-text body where applicable, then choose Find matches again, or select the intended destinations and choose Save to Chron logs.

An Outbound Email Failed or Cannot Be Queued+

Confirm that the engagement has a selected contact or a speaker assigned to an active presentation with a valid email address. Open the outbound message to see which recipient failed. Correct the address if needed, then select Retry Failed Deliveries. If sending is unavailable for every message, ask an administrator to check the mail setup.

A Template Is Missing or My Changes Cannot Be Saved+

Clear the library search and check Archived. Restore a template to make it available for new emails; permanently deleted templates cannot be restored. If another session changed the template, keep a copy of your edits, reload, and compare with the current version. Use only the listed event fields with matching double braces; Presentation schedule is allowed in the message only.

A Speaker Is Missing from Email Recipients+

Check that the speaker is assigned to an active presentation on this engagement. Add or correct their email on the speaker record, then reload the composer and select the speaker. Archived presentations do not supply recipients. Putting a speaker's name in template text does not select that person as a recipient.

A Calendar Stopped Refreshing+

Check whether that device’s subscription is still Active. A revoked URL cannot be recovered; create a new device-specific link and replace the old subscription in the calendar application.

An Event or Task Is Missing from the Month Calendar+

Confirm the displayed month and selector. Events does not include tasks, My Tasks includes only work assigned to you, and task views include only active tasks with due dates. Use Everything when you want events and all due-dated work together.

Changing the Caller Did Not Move Existing Tasks+

The Caller is used only to choose the owner of the initial standard checklist when the engagement is created. Later Caller changes do not alter existing task ownership. If responsibility changes, reassign those tasks in the Work Queue.

A QR Code Will Not Copy+

Use the PNG or SVG download links to save a generated code. You can also select the QR preview to copy it; if clipboard access is unavailable, the application opens a preview. Save the presentation first if its QR codes are not yet available.

The Speaker Notes QR Code Is Missing+

Open the engagement for editing, check the speaker selected for that presentation, and choose a Speaker Notes PDF. Save the engagement before looking for the code. A code is not shown when there is no saved PDF for that speaker. If an upload is too large, reduce the PDF to 100 MB or less; when adding several files, keep the combined upload under 120 MB.

A Save Reports an Expired Request+

Reload the page and repeat the change. MOED rejects stale or missing request tokens, and concurrent edits may require you to reopen the newest record before saving.

I Was Signed Out Unexpectedly+

Password changes, password recovery, administrator resets, account changes, deactivation, and database restoration invalidate existing sessions by design. Sign in again with the current credentials or contact an administrator if the account is unavailable.

01

Record the Why

Chron should preserve the decision and context a future teammate needs, not just “called.”

02

Name the Next Action

Turn commitments into tasks with an owner and date while the conversation is fresh.

03

Archive Before Deleting

Relationship history and event outcomes are usually more valuable than a perfectly tidy active list.

04

Protect Private Links

Calendar URLs, invitation links, verification links, recovery links, and recovery codes are credentials.
